title: Women veterans directory (national, state, territory and VA facility roles)
note: Merges the 50-state research report with the Women Veterans module v1.1.0. Crisis contacts are NOT listed here: they live once, in config/crisis_floor.yaml, and the API re-injects them into every directory response. Individual staff names and personal email addresses are deliberately excluded (CLAUDE.md: no real PII in public datasets); office lines, program URLs and role mailboxes are kept. Dedupe key is (organization, place), never phone alone (WV defect A-7).

care_types.label: Discharge upgrade and character of discharge

facility_roles.name: Women Veteran Program Manager (every VA medical center)
facility_roles.note: Advocate and coordinator for women veterans at the facility.

facility_roles.name: VHA MST Coordinator (every VA health care facility)
facility_roles.note: Point of contact for MST-related care.

facility_roles.name: VBA MST Outreach Coordinators (male and female, every VA regional office)
facility_roles.note: Claims-side contact for MST-related disability claims.

facility_roles.name: Intimate Partner Violence Assistance Program Coordinator
facility_roles.note: Services named in the source: RISE (up to 8 sessions brief counseling), Strength at Home (12-week group), sexual-violence recovery groups, safety planning, referrals to shelters and legal aid.

facility_roles.name: Maternity Care Coordinator (every VA)
facility_roles.note: Support from start of pregnancy to 12 months postpartum since 2023-10-01 per VA News; see statistic stat.wv.mcc_window.

facility_roles.name: VBA Women Veteran Coordinator (every regional office)

national.name: VA Women Veterans Call Center (WVCC)
national.eligibility_note: All-female staff; free and confidential call, text or chat. Routes to the local Women Veteran Program Manager. Hours stated by the source: Mon–Fri 8am–10pm ET, Sat 8am–6:30pm ET.

national.name: VA Center for Women Veterans
national.eligibility_note: Policy and advocacy office established by Congress in Nov 1994 (PL 103-446); not a direct-care provider.

national.name: VHA Office of Women's Health
national.eligibility_note: Sets national women's health policy.

national.name: Vet Centers (300+ community counseling centers)
national.eligibility_note: Free confidential readjustment counseling including MST and combat trauma. Phone is the Vet Center Call Center (1-877-WAR-VETS).

national.name: National Center for PTSD — care for women veterans
national.eligibility_note: Every VAMC has a PTSD specialty team or specialist (CPT, PE, EMDR).

national.name: VA Mental Health Residential Rehabilitation (RRTP) locator
national.eligibility_note: About 250 residential programs at about 120 sites (6,500+ beds) per the source. Use this locator to confirm any program in mst_residential_programs before showing it.

national.name: HUD-VASH
national.eligibility_note: HUD Housing Choice Voucher plus VA case management. Source states: no time limit; income cap 80% of Area Median Income; registered sex offenders ineligible; apply through a VA medical center or the homeless call center in the crisis floor.

national.name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
national.eligibility_note: VA grants to nonprofits for rapid re-housing and homelessness prevention for very low-income veteran families (since 2011).

national.name: Military OneSource
national.eligibility_note: Childcare resources and referrals for eligible members. Post-separation access window is modelled separately (see transition timeline).

national.name: Child Care Aware of America — DoD MCCYN / MCCYN-PLUS fee assistance
national.eligibility_note: Primarily active-duty, Guard and Reserve members, not general veterans.
national.caveat: Eligibility must be flagged in the app; most veterans will not qualify.

national.name: Service Women's Action Network (SWAN)
national.eligibility_note: 24/7 assistance hotline (888-502-8755); case management (301-578-2049, casemanager@servicewomen.org); office (202) 798-5570; advocacy and pro-bono legal referrals. Founded 2007.

national.name: Protect Our Defenders
national.eligibility_note: MST advocacy and legal help.

national.name: Cohen Veterans Network
national.eligibility_note: Free or low-cost therapy for post-9/11 veterans and families; accepts TRICARE; telehealth. Clinic list in cohen_clinics.

national.name: Headstrong Project
national.eligibility_note: Free trauma-focused therapy (CPT, EMDR, PE); first 30 sessions cost-free; intake response within 2 business days. States listed by the source: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, ID, IL, MD, NJ, NY, NC, OR, PA, TX, VA, WA, plus DC.
national.caveat: Source says 15 states + DC but lists 16 states (conflict.wv.headstrong_state_count).

national.name: Wounded Warrior Project — Women Warriors Initiative
national.eligibility_note: WWP Talk (weekly one-to-one calls), Project Odyssey (12 weeks), Warrior Care Network; funds women-veteran MST programs.

national.name: Give an Hour
national.eligibility_note: Free mental health care through volunteer providers in every state; serves regardless of discharge status per the source.

national.name: Final Salute Inc.
national.eligibility_note: H.O.M.E. transitional housing (up to 2 years, includes childcare subsidy) and S.A.F.E. emergency financial assistance. Honorable or under-honorable discharge; others case by case. Founded Nov 2010; source reports 8,000+ women veterans served across 30 states and territories.

national.name: U.S.VETS ADVANCE Women's Program
national.eligibility_note: Women veterans including those with children: sexual-trauma treatment, substance-use treatment, work re-entry. Sites named: Long Beach CA, Barber's Point HI, Phoenix AZ (women's wing opened 2026). Also runs Women Vets on Point (national navigation).

national.name: Volunteers of America — women veteran housing
national.eligibility_note: Women veteran housing in multiple states.

national.name: National Coalition for Homeless Veterans (NCHV)
national.eligibility_note: Policy and technical-assistance hub; coordinates the Stand Down Registry.
national.caveat: Distinct from the VA National Call Center for Homeless Veterans in the crisis floor.

national.name: Operation Homefront
national.eligibility_note: Family financial and relief programs.

national.name: Blue Star Families
national.eligibility_note: Chapters nationwide; family support and research (Military Family Lifestyle Survey).

national.name: V-WISE (IVMF, Syracuse University)
national.eligibility_note: Women veterans, active-duty women, and women military spouses or partners. Three weeks online plus a three-day conference. Source states a $75 fee and 3,800+ graduates.

national.name: Women Veterans Interactive Foundation (WVIF)
national.eligibility_note: National 501(c)(3); Operation Safety Net and transition assistance.

national.name: AcademyWomen
national.eligibility_note: Leadership and mentoring.

national.name: Dress for Success
national.eligibility_note: Professional attire through partnerships.

national.name: Minority Veterans of America
national.eligibility_note: Women, veterans of color, LGBTQ+ and religious-minority veterans; case management and housing at its community center (King County, WA). Takes no federal funding.

national.name: Disabled American Veterans (DAV)
national.eligibility_note: Free claims help from accredited representatives; 38 Transition Service Officers at 109+ installations in 2024 per the TAP report.

national.name: The American Legion and VFW — women veteran committees
national.eligibility_note: Benefits assistance nationwide from accredited service officers. Referral must name the representative the veteran chooses (rule R5).

national.name: Team Red White & Blue; Team Rubicon
national.eligibility_note: Community, physical and service engagement (co-ed).

national.name: Grace After Fire
national.eligibility_note: Texas-based peer support (Table Talk), STARS financial resiliency, wellness retreat.

national.name: Foundation for Women Warriors
national.eligibility_note: Childcare assistance, emergency financial help, professional development; Southern California focus; established 1920.

eligibility_highlights.statement: VA provides free care for physical and mental health conditions related to MST. Per the source, no service connection, disability rating, minimum length of service, report or documentation of the event is required, and most former members with OTH or uncharacterized discharges qualify; former Guard/Reserve qualify with federal active-duty service or a service-connected disability.
Maternity Care Coordinator support runs from the start of pregnancy to 12 months postpartum, effective 2023-10-01 (previously ended 8 weeks postpartum).
eligibility_highlights.verify_against: VA News, Office of Women's Health
